_comment: Indexed by TerrainTyper.Type. Order is load-bearing — do not reorder without changing the enum. blocker_h is meters of LOS-opaque cover above ground level; note that visibility.turret_h_m is 2.6, so cover below that height does not block a tank's line of sight at all on level ground — it is the threshold the tiers are chosen around, not a smooth dial. The per-type `spotting` scalar that used to live here has been replaced by concealment_classes below — see docs/decisions/0028.
_forest_tiers_comment: The tiers are appended rather than inserted next to woods because these indices are raw array offsets — TerrainTyper.Type indexes straight into types, and inserting at 3 would silently repaint every map. woods_light's 2.2 m is chosen against visibility.turret_h_m (2.6) and hull_h_m (1.4), not picked for looks: LOS blocks when a tile's cover rises above the observer's eye line, and the eye is ground + turret_h. Cover below 2.6 m therefore blocks a tank's sightline not at all, while cover above 1.4 m still masks a target's hull — so light woods is concealment that hides the hull and leaves the turret, which is the state this game is named after. Above 2.6 m the tier is simply opaque and 3 m occludes exactly as thoroughly as 8 m does. It is a threshold, not a dial.
_concealment_comment: How hard it is to SEE a unit standing on each terrain type, as a multiplier on the observing side's optical range — spotting is deterministic and this is one of its three modifiers (docs/decisions/0024). Indexed by MovementClass.Kind, and each `values` array is parallel to types above; both orders are load-bearing, exactly as in movement_classes. Per class rather than per type because concealment is the one visibility number that is not a property of the ground alone: a tank in heavy forest is a tank wedged between trunks it cannot fit through, and a rifle section in the same stand is invisible. Making that a data axis now is what lets infantry land later without touching code. Config slices the tracked row out as terrain_spotting, which is what almost every caller means — the same relationship terrain_move_cost has to class_move_cost, and for the same reason. The tracked row is numerically identical to the per-type `spotting` scalar it replaces, so the restructure changed no behavior for the iteration-2 roster; tests/test_config pins that against a literal. A class that omits a terrain pads to 1.0 — fully visible — which is the opposite of the movement table's impassable padding and for the same reason: nobody-decided must not read as invisible.
_movement_classes_comment: Movement cost per (class, terrain type). Indexed by MovementClass.Kind, and each costs array is parallel to types above — both orders are load-bearing. A cost is a multiplier on the base step cost; -1 means impassable to that class. This is the single source of truth for going: there is deliberately no per-type move_cost field, because two places to write the same number is one place to get it wrong. The road row is not a tile type — no tile is ever assigned it (see docs/decisions/0011). It is the made surface: the cost of a step that runs along a road link, and the cost of standing on a road tile whose natural ground the class could not otherwise enter, which is what makes a bridge deck drivable.
